Molecular Biology & Genomics: Using sequencing techniques for comprehensive characterization and surveillance on genetic diversity within virus populations; study pathogenicity differences between strains isolated from different geographic locations or vectors. 3.Mathematical Modeling: Utilizing computational simulations to predict ZIKV spread patterns, evaluate the effectiveness of vector control measures under various scenarios (e.g., timing & frequency), as well model potential outcomes with and without intervention strategies. 4. Laboratory Studies: Investigating infection dynamics in mosquitoes using a combination approaches including viral load quantification techniques such as RT-qPCR. texts.full_text: d-brain barriera (BBB), which is formed by endothelial cells lining the brain vasculature and that are linked by tight junctions^[@CR15]^. Tight junctions limit the paracellular diffusion of molecules from the bloodstream into the brain, thereby forming a physical barrier. The BBB is furthermore maintained by efflux transporters such as P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and multidrug resistance-associated proteins (MRPs) that actively pump small molecules out of the brain, and by influx transporters such as organic cation transporters (OCTs) and organic anion transporters (OATs) that actively pump small molecules into the brain^[@CR16]--[@CR18]^. As a result, the brain penetration of a compound depends on its size, charge, polarity, lipophilicity, and ability to interact with BBB transporters^[@CR19]--[@CR21]^. For example, small neutral molecules are able to passively diffuse across the BBB, whereas larger, charged and polar molecules need to be actively transported into the brain. As a result, compounds that are small, neutral and lipophilic tend to have better brain penetration compared to large, charged and polar compounds^[@CR20]--[@CR22]^. Moreover, compounds that interact with efflux transporters such as P-gp and MRPs tend to have lower brain penetration compared to compounds that do not interact with these transporters^[@CR23]--[@CR25]^. As a result, compounds that are actively transported into the brain by BBB influx transporters, but that do not interact with efflux transporters, tend to have the best brain penetration^[@CR20],[@CR26]--[@CR28]$.
